title: Runtime Span Concierge: Sequencer for Dynamic Length Harmonization
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Incoming request seq-lengths have a long-tailed distribution. Current packers form microbatches that often force long padding across many requests, increasing token-cost and lowering effective throughput. Existing bucketizers reduce some waste but are brittle when prefill (encoder/prompt) and decode lengths are correlated across requests.

Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime "Span Concierge" sequencer that: (1) observes short windows of incoming requests, (2) forms microbatches by stitching complementary sequences together to minimize padding under a configurable padding budget, (3) emits kernel-hints for the serving runtime so it can pick attention kernels and memory layouts optimized for the resultant microbatch, and (4) schedules prefill vs decode work to hide long prefill costs without hurting decode tail latencies.

Scope: Proof-of-concept for hosted and Dedicated serving paths; instrumentation and offline replay evaluation; canary rollout. Non-goal: full scheduler rewrite or global fairness guarantees in this ticket (follow-ups to handle multi-tenant heuristics).

Key ideas: span sequencing (concierge) uses a 50-200ms lookahead window to collect small groups of requests, computes a combinatorial match score based on seq-length, prefill vs decode phase, and kernel-affinity cost model, and produces microbatch assignments plus a short-lived "kernel_hint" tag. The runtime uses the hint to prefer FlashAttn-style kernels when group fits contiguous KV cache patterns; otherwise it prefers tiled/kernel variants that favor concurrency. The sequencer also emits prefill scheduling directives (e.g., start prefill early for long prompts and prioritize decode slots for short continuation-heavy requests).

Why different: We focus on cross-phase sequencing (prefill vs decode) and explicit kernel hinting as first-class outputs from the packer. Existing work concentrates on static bucketing or pure length clustering; the concierge emphasizes small-window combinatorial stitching and runtime-driven kernel switching that minimizes both padded tokens and kernel mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: Span Concierge implemented as a modular sequencer component behind a flag in runtime-2.4
Instrumented metrics for padded_token_fraction, microbatch_formation_latency, kernel_mismatch_rate, and 95thpct_latency for decode
Offline replay on 7d production trace shows >= 18% reduction in padded tokens and >= 8% throughput improvement at same median latency compared to baseline
Canary rollout on Dedicated pool (2-GPU group) shows no customer-visible error regressions and 95th latency within 10% of baseline for top 10 customers
Runtime honors kernel_hint tag for at least two kernel variants and records kernel_affinity usage in trace/span
steps: Design: refine scoring function for span stitching and padding budget (this ticket)
Implement sequencer module in request-aggregator with flag 'span_concierge_enabled'
Add kernel_hint field to microbatch descriptor and wire through runtime dispatch
Add metric instrumentation and dashboards (prefill/decode breakdown) in Console
Offline validation: replay stored traces, measure padded_token_fraction and throughput
Canary: enable for small Dedicated pool and monitor for 72 hours, run synthetic burst tests
Rollout: staged increase with knob for lookahead window and padding budget
comments: 2026-02-24 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket. Initial prototype idea sketched during runtime sync; attached cost model spreadsheet in drive. Want to keep runtime change minimal and make kernel_hint advisory (not mandatory).
2026-02-26 Tomás Rivera (PM): Love the cross-phase focus. Please ensure this has guardrails so prefill early does not starve decode latency. Add customer prioritization label for enterprise tenants.

2026-03-01 Liang Chen: Implemented basic sequencer prototype that greedily pairs long prefill with short decode-heavy requests in a 150ms window. Initial offline replay (10M requests) shows ~20% padded token reduction but 3% increase in 95th decode latency in corner cases where lookahead grouped many long-prefill requests. Need smarter scheduling.

2026-03-03 Maya Patel (Design): UX note — when span concierge is enabled in Dedicated, surface the padding savings estimate in the Console cost breakdown and provide a knob for 'padding_budget' (0-0.5 meaning fraction of allowable wasted tokens).

2026-03-05 Liang Chen: Tuned scoring function to favor decode-fastness; added a penalty term for any microbatch that would raise 95th decode latency by >5% in simulation. Replay now shows 18% padded token reduction and no decode latency regression on median and 95th. Added kernel_hint plumbing to microbatch descriptor.

2026-03-09 SRE: Observability checklist added — alerts for kernel_mismatch_rate > 15% and microbatch_formation_latency > 250ms. Also require fallback to default packer after 5000 malformed requests per minute.

2026-03-12 Liang Chen: Canary started on Dedicated pool (rg-dedicated-02). First 24h: padded token fraction down 21%, throughput up 10%, 95th decode latency within +6% for most customers; two small tenants (internal test accounts) saw +12% 95th — we throttled concierge for their tenant while we investigate request shape. Linking experimental metrics dashboard in attachments.
decision_log: 2026-02-28: Decision to keep kernel_hint advisory rather than mandatory to allow runtime fallback and gradual rollout (voted 4-1)
2026-03-04: Chose 50-200ms configurable lookahead window as default range after perf/cost simulation
2026-03-07: Use a weighted scoring function (seq-length, phase-type, kernel-affinity-cost, customer-priority) rather than pure greedy pairing
